title: geogen glTF node extras, version 1
description: Gameplay metadata geogen writes to glTF node extras under the 'geogen' key. This file is the whole contract: the exporter writes a node meta key only when it is declared here (src/geogen/extras.py; build-only keys are registered there and never exported), so 'geogen' takes no other keys. runtime/godot/README.md lists which runtime script reads each key.

uid.description: Stable ID: '<package>:<authored path>' (cottage:house/door), from the names things were authored with, never the exported node name. Present on placed assets and scenes, tagged or typed nodes and anything with interactions. Content and saved state refer to nodes by it, so it survives a re-export; <name>.refs.json beside the manifest lists every one.

tags.description: Semantic tags, dotted from general to specific (room, room.hotel_bedroom, furniture.bed, door.interior).

type.description: Special node kinds. room_volume: axis-aligned box (in the node's frame) of size 'size' centred on the node. spawn: player start, facing the node's +Z. collider: collision-only geometry (Godot suffix -colonly = trimesh, -convcolonly = convex); do not render. material_group: helper node whose primitives were folded into its parent's mesh (left unreferenced). npc: a character placed here (see 'npc'); its body asset is the child named by npc.body.node. vehicle: a vehicle asset root (see 'vehicle'). place: a named trigger volume (see 'place'). light: the <node>_light child carrying a fixture's KHR_lights_punctual light. lod: a <node>_LOD<n> level of its parent's mesh (see 'level', 'ratio'). traffic: the root of a moving fleet (see 'fleet'); its children are the starting vehicles. train: a train (see 'train'); its children are the consist.

shape.description: Collider nodes only: how the collision geometry was made.

collider.description: Mesh nodes: the collider chosen for this mesh (none = no collision). The collider itself is a child node.

level.description: type lod only: the LOD level, 1 = the first reduction (the node is named <node>_LOD<level>).

ratio.description: type lod only: the share of the full mesh's triangles this level was decimated to.

walkable.description: Surface meant to be walked on (navmesh input).

room.description: Room identity, on room nodes and their room_volume.

door.description: Door/opening nodes generated by floor plans.

joint.description: Articulation pivot (e.g. a door leaf's hinge): children rotate about 'axis' (node frame) between min_deg and max_deg.

clips.description: Skeletal animation clips over the joints below this node. Each is a glTF animation named 'animation' (<node>_<clip>; engines may mangle '/') targeting the joint nodes (Skeleton3D bones in Godot); 'loop' clips repeat.

speed.description: Locomotion clips: the ground speed (m/s) the cycle was made for; scale playback by actual speed / this.

rests.description: Pose clips: the hands (IK end bones) resting on a support in this pose, a table top or a sill, made for a default height: a runtime may move them onto the support that is really there.

from.description: Transition clips (sit_down, stand_up, ...): the pose the clip starts in.

to.description: Transition clips: the pose the clip ends in. Play the clip when changing pose from 'from' to 'to'.

root.description: Transition clips: the body root's path while the clip plays, in the frame of where the character ends up (the affordance anchor; the approach point when 'to' is stand), x right, y up, z forward. Made for the action's default approach offset and seat height: blend the difference to the actual start and end placements over the clip.

interactions.description: Asset nodes: state machines that move descendant nodes (by exported node name). Exported transforms show the 'initial' state; a part's rest pose is M(initial value)^-1 * its exported transform, and its pose for value v is asset * M(v) * rest, where M rotates by v degrees about 'axis' through 'pivot' (asset frame) or translates v metres along 'axis'. use() goes to states[target].next; 'then' auto-advances on arrival; 'emit' names an event raised on arrival.

targets.description: Nodes the player aims at to use it.

refused.description: What the prompt says, and a refused use tells the user, while the interaction's `when` (in the manifest's state) is false.

reach.description: Metres from the eye its targets can be used from, when that is further than the player's reach (absent: the player's).

lock.description: While locked, use() fails; holders of 'key' can lock/unlock.

after.description: Dwell before 'then' (auto-close): seconds, or {minutes: n} of clock time (the rules program moves it on).

type.description: rotate: values in degrees about axis through pivot; translate: metres along axis; visible: 1 shown, 0 hidden (with their colliders), no axis or pivot.

footprint.description: Furniture: floor footprint [x, z] in metres (asset frame, centred on the origin).

clearance.description: Furniture: free space needed beyond the footprint on each side (front = +Z), metres.

light.description: Light fixtures: an omni light at 'offset' (node frame). Exported as a KHR_lights_punctual point light on a <node>_light child (intensity = energy * 12 cd).

auto.description: night: switched by the runtime's world clock (on after dark), not by a switch.

affordances.description: Things an actor can do at an asset (asset frame): sit/lie/use/stand/look at 'position' facing 'yaw' degrees about +Y (0 = +Z); 'height' is where the hips rest. The player takes sit/lie; NPCs run 'action' (assets/npcs/actions.yaml), starting from 'approach' (floor level), for 'duration' seconds, adding 'advertises' to their needs; 'slots' actors at once; 'interaction' is the asset interaction a use step drives.

depth.description: sit: how far in front of 'position' the seat's front edge is, metres. With the body pose's 'reach' it keeps the sitter's calves clear of the seat.

portal.description: A doorway NPC paths may cross (asset frame): width x height opening centred on 'center', 'depth' thick along 'normal'. A path through it while 'interaction' isn't in state 'open' runs the NPC 'pass' action (stop 'clearance' beyond the near face, open, walk through, maybe close).

swing.description: The side the leaf opens toward: front (+normal) or back.

handles.description: The handle on each side (front: +normal), its middle in the asset frame as the door stands when exported. An NPC reaches for the one on its side to open the door; on the side the leaf swings away from it stands close enough to hold it as it opens.

place.description: type place only: a named trigger volume (geogen/places.py). The node is the middle of the volume's bottom and the volume rises along its +Y: a box of 'size' [x, y, z], or the footprint 'polygon' ([x, z] points in the node's frame) extruded 'height'. Actors (the player, NPCs) entering and leaving it are events whose subject is the node's uid.

detect.description: What the place reports, when not only actors: with 'props', physics props in it count too, and the runtime keeps its 'occupants' state (the number of things in it).

sink.description: Spawned items (geogen/flows.py) entering it are taken in: only those named in 'accepts' (empty: any). The runtime keeps its 'received' state (how many) and raises 'received' {item, ...the item's data}.

physics.description: A physics prop (geogen/physics.py): the node and everything under it are one rigid body, a box of 'size' centred at 'center' (the node's frame), or with 'shape' a sphere of 'radius' or an upright capsule of 'radius' and 'height' (end to end) centred there. 'damping' slows it (linear, angular: per second). The parts' own colliders are not used. 'carry': the player can pick it up. 'spawn_at' (the node's frame): where its 'spawn' interaction puts it on going live; stowed, it is hidden and out of the simulation, and a live prop that falls out of the world is stowed.

flows.description: Spawned items (geogen/flows.py). 'track': see below. 'source': this asset makes copies of the item templates among its descendants (nodes with 'item') while it runs: 'rate' a second, and at once for each one its 'queued' state asks for, while it has fewer than 'max_alive' in the world and has made fewer than 'count' (0: no limit). They appear at 'at' (this node's frame), up to 'spread' m off it across x and z, physics items moving at 'velocity' (this node's frame). Its state: running, queued (rules set them), emitted and alive (the runtime drives them); signal emitted {item}.

items.description: What it makes: none yet for a waves source built alone (its waves are read when it is placed).

item.description: The item file, relative to assets/.

name.description: The item's name: its template's 'item.name' (absent: the asset was built alone, with no templates).

waves.description: Instead of items at a rate: while running, wave by wave. A wave starts 'delay' s after the source runs; its groups go out in order, 'count' items of 'name' each 'gap' s apart; when all of the wave's items are gone it is cleared (signal wave_cleared {wave}), and the source stops (running false) unless 'auto'. After the last, all_cleared. State 'wave' counts them. A file name: the asset was built alone (no waves read).

effector.description: Acts on track items in 'range' m of 'at' (this node's frame), 'rate' times a second while its 'enabled' state is true: 'effect' damage (items with data.hp lose that much; at 0 they are destroyed and their source raises killed {item, ...data}) or take (the item goes; its 'taken' state counts, signal took). 'targets': first (furthest along), last, nearest, strongest (most hp); 'accepts' limits it to those items. 'aim' parts (exported node names) turn toward the target, yaw about their Y and pitch about their X, 'turn_rate' deg/s; 'projectile' is what a shot looks like (damage lands as it fires).

track.description: A path items follow: 'points' (this node's frame, every 0.25 m) 'length' m long. belt: items move at 'speed' together and queue; walk: each at its own item speed; roll: gravity drives each from 'speed' ((5/7) g sin(slope), less 'damping' per second), and they spin (physics items too: they fall off a 'drop' end as bodies). Items keep 'spacing' (or their radii) apart. 'end': auto (on to the track whose start is within 0.5 m of this end, else a sink), sink (take them in: 'received' state and signal, only 'accepts' items when listed), stop (they wait there), drop (they fall off as physics bodies). A source whose spawn point is within 0.5 m of a track's start puts its items on it. Its state: running (inputs start / stop), received.

item.description: An item template (geogen/flows.py): not part of the world (the runtime takes it out on load) but what its source copies. 'mode': physics (a rigid body, from this node's 'physics'), belt or walk (along a track). 'data' is what each copy carries; 'lifetime' and 'stuck' (s) take a copy away (0: never). 'gait' is how a walk item's body steps: it bobs 'bob' m twice a 'stride' (m), rocks 'sway' degrees side to side and swings its heading 'waddle' degrees.

travel.description: A travel point (geogen/travel.py): 'use' it (its 'travel' interaction emits 'travel') or walk into 'volume' (asset frame, on: enter) to go to spawn 'spawn' (default: the first) of catalogue scene 'scene' (absent: this scene). 'target' names the part aimed at for on: use.

poses.description: Character body assets: named poses as root transforms relative to an anchor (offset m, rotation deg XYZ, scale).

npc.description: A placed NPC, fully resolved from assets/npcs/<definition>.yaml: everything the runtime interpreter needs. Distances in metres, rates per second. 'home.polygon' is [x, z] in this node's frame.

body.description: The body: an 'asset' file or a character 'archetype' (with the person drawn as 'character'), built with 'params', placed as the child 'node'; 'poses' are its root transforms per pose.

owns.description: Stable IDs of the things only this NPC uses (an affordance under one is refused to others); it likes them best.

prefers.description: Stable IDs of things it likes best (an affordance under one scores higher), still free for others.

work.description: Stable ID of where its routine's 'at: work' blocks keep it: their options are the affordances under it, wherever that is from home.

affordance_tags.description: Only affordances with one of these tags (empty: any).

wander.description: Where go_to: random goes: points on up-facing surfaces of nodes with these tags (empty: the home region).

routine.description: Time-of-day blocks ('from' / 'to' in hours, wrapping midnight): while one is active its 'activities' and 'preferences' multiply scores, and 'away' sends the NPC off (the leave action) until it ends.

at.description: work: the block's options are the affordances under the NPC's 'work'.

attention.description: How it notices the player (geogen/npc.py ATTENTION_DEFAULTS); a part left out is off. look: head look-at within 'range' m and a 'cone' of degrees, turning up to 'yaw' / 'pitch' degrees at 'speed'. greet: on E it raises 'signal' (not twice within 'debounce' s) and, standing, runs 'action' (waving at most every 'cooldown' s), looking at the greeter 'acknowledge' s. yield: steps 'step' m aside ('action') from a player walking at it within 'distance' m.

container.description: Storage: how many items it holds, and which part is the storage volume.

nav.description: false on rooms/room volumes that aren't meant to be walked (lift shafts); playtests skip them.

size.description: room_volume only: box size in metres [x, y, z].

city.description: City district root (geogen/layout/city.py): the block grid and the district's extent in metres.

block.description: City block: its grid index [i, j].

lot.description: City lot: the block it is in, its zone, the block side it fronts and its rectangle [x0, z0, x1, z1] in the city frame.

building.description: A building root: its storey count and height in metres. A building a city placed on a lot also has the catalogue 'entry' it was drawn from (a recipe name or asset file stem) and its 'zone'.

street_furniture.description: Kind of street furniture: lamp, tree, bench, hydrant, ...

lod.description: Root of a chunk's exterior LOD stand-in: decimated to 'ratio' of its triangles, parts smaller than 'min_size' metres dropped.

interior.description: Root of a streamed building interior chunk: the building (by name) it belongs to.

signal.description: A traffic signal head: the intersection and phase it shows and the lane it faces (ids of the manifest's traffic section). The runtime lights its lamp_red | lamp_amber | lamp_green parts from that intersection's cycle. With 'crossing' it is a pedestrian head: the runtime lights lamp_walk or lamp_dont from that entry of the traffic section's pedestrian_signals.

crossing.description: Pedestrian heads: the id of the pedestrian signal (a crosswalk's walk and clearance intervals) they show.

character.description: A person drawn from a character archetype (geogen/characters.py): the archetype (a '/'-joined chain when variants hand the draw on) and the seed that picked them.

stairs.description: A flight of stairs (geogen/generators/stairs.py). Spiral stairs add 'ends', where you step on at the bottom and off at the top (node frame): a runtime should link them on its navigation map, since a self-overlapping spiral's navmesh comes out in pieces; 'path' is the walking line between them, for bodies that follow the link.

water.description: A water sheet (geogen/generators/water.py): what a water shader needs; every key is optional and a runtime has its own defaults. Colours are linear RGB.

depth_scale.description: Depth in metres over which shallow turns to deep.

driving.description: A vehicle of a moving fleet (a child of a type traffic node): where it starts on the lane graph. 'lane' is a lane id of the manifest's traffic section, 's' metres along it, 'factor' this driver's share of the lane speed.

fleet.description: type traffic only: how its vehicles drive (geogen/traffic.py, from a kind: traffic definition). 'count' vehicles, 'spacing' metres apart at the start; 'driving' is the IDM car-following model; 'turns' weights the choice at intersections; 'yield' lists who they stop for; 'schedule' is [[hour, share of the fleet on the road], ...] over the day.

headway.description: Seconds kept behind the vehicle ahead.

give_up.description: Seconds held on green before picking another exit.

train.description: type train only: a train and its precomputed run (geogen/trains.py). 'railway' is a railway id of the manifest's traffic.railways. 'run' is the distance along the line of the train's middle every 'dt' seconds for one departure ('duration' seconds long); departures repeat every timetable.headway from timetable.offset. 'stops' are when it stands at each station and 'closures' the [from, to] times each level crossing is shut, all in seconds from departure. 'cars' are the consist (child node names), each 'offset' metres from the train's middle with its bogie pivots (z in the car's frame).

warning.description: Seconds a crossing closes before the train reaches it.

vehicle.description: A vehicle asset (geogen/vehicles.py), built along +Z with its origin on the ground midway between the axles. Parts named here are descendants of this node: wheels spin about their local X (radius in metres), steer parts turn, paint parts carry the tint, lamps glow by kind. clearance is [length, width, height]; front/rear are the bumper z positions.

bogie_centers.description: Rail: z of each bogie's pivot (vehicle frame).

sound.description: Synthesised sound hooks: engine {base Hz, per_speed Hz per m/s, volume_db, roughness}, horn {tones Hz, seconds, volume_db}.

params.description: An asset's params, as it was built with them: a map, not a fixed set of keys (each asset declares its own).

npc_step.description: One step of an NPC action (assets/npcs/actions.yaml): exactly one verb, with options 'at' (where a pose is held), 'hold' (a pose step: the skeletal pose clip pose_<hold> to hold instead of the pose's own, where the body has it) and 'if' (a flag it needs).

reach.description: sit: z of the back of the calves below the seat, relative to the anchor, metres (compare an affordance's 'depth').
